stories.label: Indonesia rescuers search for 140 people from stricken ferry
stories.summary: The KM Virgo Transport 8 left Surabaya for Banjarmasin carrying 243 people and lost contact in the Java Sea early Sunday in bad weather; one confirmed dead, about 140 still missing, 103 evacuated per Antara. Lead with the manifest against the rescue count, because the gap is the story and the manifest itself is usually the first thing that turns out to be wrong — Indonesian ferry casualty figures routinely rise when unticketed passengers are counted. Mechanism for the reader: Indonesia is 17,000 islands with no alternative to sea transport for ordinary people, so ferry safety is not a transport question but an access question — overloading, ageing hulls and weather-window pressure are the predictable output of a route that must sail because there is no other way to get to Kalimantan. Report the vessel's age, class, operator and licensed capacity, what the Surabaya port authority cleared it to carry, what BMKG had forecast, and how long it took SAR to reach the position. Then the accountability layer: Indonesia's transport ministry has promised the same reforms after Tanjung Priok, after the Sewol-era audits, after the 2018 Lake Toba sinking — name what was promised and what was done. Who is affected: working-class inter-island passengers and migrant workers, not tourists. Indonesia is an OIC member and Antara News (ID) is in the cluster — use it for the domestic figures rather than resting on DW and US News, since the national agency has the SAR and Basarnas numbers first. NOTE: the feed contained a second cluster for this same event mis-titled 'Altman Says OpenAI Will Not Go Public in 2026' (eng-12005379, Bloomberg) — the Bloomberg URL is genuine ferry reporting and is merged into sources here; the two clusters are one event. Fills the audit's flagged Southeast Asia gap, which had been absent outright.

stories.label: Protest continues in Karachi as family refuses to bury teen until his killers are arrested
stories.summary: Six robbers, two of them in police uniforms, entered Roidad Hussain's house in Manghopir on 8 September and shot his teenage son dead; five days on the family will not bury him until the killers are arrested, and a DIG has confirmed the protest. Lead with the unburied body, because in Islamic practice burial is owed within a day — a family that holds a funeral open for five days is making the only sanction available to people the state will not answer. Mechanism, and this is the systemic point rather than a crime brief: the two police uniforms are the whole case. Karachi's uniform supply is unregulated and open-market, and the uniform works as a weapon precisely because a household opens the door to it — so the question for the Sindh police is not only who fired but who can buy the uniform, and whether any serving officer was involved, which is the allegation the family is actually making. Report the boy's name, what the FIR says and when it was registered, which police station, whether any arrest has followed, and what the DIG and the Edhi Foundation have said. Then the structural why: Manghopir is a peripheral, largely Pashtun and Baloch working-class katchi abadi, the part of Karachi where policing is thinnest and extortion densest, and the class geography of who gets an investigation is the reason this protest exists. Pakistan is an OIC member and Dawn (PK) is the regional outlet doing the original reporting — attribute to it throughout. Do not write this as a crime story; write it as a story about what recourse looks like when there is none.

stories.label: US court blocks Trump administration plan to cut disaster agency workforce
stories.summary: US District Judge Susan Illston ruled on Friday that DHS acted unlawfully in ordering job cuts at FEMA. Lead with the legal finding, not the politics: a court has held that the executive cannot dismantle a congressionally created agency by staffing decision. Mechanism, and it is the precedent our reader should take: Congress appropriates for an agency and sets its statutory duties, but the executive controls hiring, so a reduction-in-force is the instrument by which an administration can nullify a law it cannot repeal — Illston's ruling tests whether that instrument is reviewable, and she is the same judge who has now blocked this manoeuvre across several agencies. Report what the order actually does (injunction scope, which positions, whether cuts already executed are reversed), the statutory hook she relied on, and what the administration's appeal path is. Then the consequence, which is not abstract: FEMA is the agency that staffs disaster declarations, and hurricane season is running — report current staffing against the pre-cut baseline and against the number of open declarations. Accountability: name the DHS officials who ordered it. This is the 'single court ruling with precedent' case, not a news-cycle item — keep it on the mechanism of nullification-by-staffing, which is a pattern our readers will meet again in their own states. Al Jazeera (QA) is a reader-aligned source and is the only one in the feed cluster; the story is US-domestic so no OIC regional source applies.

stories.label: Number of local coalitions to rise steeply after 4 November
stories.summary: Susan Booysen, Wits professor emeritus, projects South Africa's hung municipalities rising from 88 to about 110 at the 4 November local elections. Lead with the two numbers, because a country where a quarter of its municipalities are governed by coalition has quietly changed its constitutional form without amending anything. Mechanism for the reader, and it is the part every horse-race story omits: South African local government uses proportional representation with no threshold and no coalition-formation rules, so a council of fifty can seat a party holding one seat, and that one seat can price a mayoralty — which is why Johannesburg has churned through mayors at a rate that makes budget execution impossible and why refuse, water and electricity delivery degrade fastest in exactly the metros with the most fragmented councils. Coalition instability is not a political inconvenience; it is a service-delivery mechanism with a body count in cholera and water outages. Report the current 88 by province, the ANC's projected share, and what the Municipal Structures Act does and does not say about coalition agreements — there is draft legislation on thresholds, so say where it stands. Then give the reader the comparative frame: this is the same arithmetic that produced Sweden's kingmaker problem, which we reported this morning, arriving in a state with far less fiscal slack to absorb it. Attribute the projection to Booysen and Daily Maverick as a forecast, not a finding. This is a South African analyst on South African politics and the audit's Africa gap is at two articles, both security — this one is governance and economics, which is what the continent has been missing here for three days.

stories.label: Iran can easily withdraw from NPT, revise nuclear doctrine
stories.summary: Abbas Goudarzi, spokesman for the Iranian parliament's presiding board, said on Sunday that leaving the Non-Proliferation Treaty is 'a readily attainable step' and that trusting the United States amounts to accepting deception. Lead with the institutional source, not the sentiment: this is the Majlis presiding board, the body that would actually carry a withdrawal bill, speaking during a war — which makes it a legislative signal rather than a talking point, and that distinction is the whole value of the story. Mechanism, and it must be precise because almost no coverage gets it right: NPT Article X permits withdrawal on three months' written notice to the other parties and the Security Council, stating the extraordinary events that jeopardised supreme interests — so withdrawal is legal, quick, and the only state ever to do it is North Korea in 2003. What withdrawal actually removes is IAEA safeguards access, meaning the world's ability to observe Iranian enrichment ends before any weapon exists; the inspectors are the thing that leaves, and that is the concrete cost. Explain also what Iran's current doctrine is — Khamenei's fatwa against nuclear weapons is the stated basis, so 'revising the doctrine' is a religious-legal claim as much as a strategic one, and our reader will want that treated seriously rather than waved at. Report what the Majlis has actually passed or tabled to date, what the IAEA's present access is, and what Araghchi and the foreign ministry say, since parliament and the ministry have diverged on this before. Iran is an OIC member and Mehr (IR) is the domestic agency reporting its own parliament — attribute plainly to Mehr as the source of a named official's statement, do not upgrade a spokesman's remark into state policy, and seek corroboration from IRNA or Tehran Times. Distinct from our 09-12 Trump-claims and 09-13 Hormuz diplomacy pieces: this is the treaty architecture, not the war or the waterway.

stories.label: Soldiers arrest three suspects after 17-year-old was killed in Plateau
stories.summary: Peter Gyang, 17, was killed at Kafi-Abu village in Barkin Ladi, Plateau State, and troops acting on intelligence arrested three suspects at a nearby settlement on Saturday. Lead with the name and the place, because Barkin Ladi is not a random location — it is the epicentre of the Plateau killings, where hundreds died in 2018 and where attacks have continued through every commission of inquiry since. Mechanism, and it is what makes this a governance story rather than a crime report: soldiers, not police, made the arrests, because Nigeria's Middle Belt has been under a standing military operation for years — Operation Safe Haven — and a state that polices with the army has replaced investigation with occupation. Soldiers can detain; they cannot build a prosecutable case, which is why the conviction record for Plateau killings is close to nothing across a decade of arrests. Report who the three are, whether they have been transferred to police custody or the DSS, and what happened to those arrested after the previous Barkin Ladi attacks — that follow-up is the story. Then the structural why for our reader: the farmer–herder framing exported to the world hides a land-tenure conflict over grazing corridors, indigene-settler citizenship rules that deny some Plateau residents state rights by birth, and a climate signal pushing pastoralists south — name those, and do not let a Muslim-versus-Christian frame stand in for them. Nigeria is an OIC member and Premium Times (NG) is the regional outlet with original reporting; attribute throughout. Second Africa entry against a gap the audit has flagged for three days.

stories.label: The Outlook Is Getting Grimmer By The Day For Oil Exports From The Red Sea
stories.summary: With Iraqi militia drones striking the Saudi East–West pipeline and Ansarallah now holding the positions that command Bab al-Mandab, every route out of Gulf and Red Sea oil is under one of two guns. Write the export map as arithmetic, not as a war narrative. Lead with the count: Saudi crude has exactly three ways to reach a buyer — Hormuz, the East–West pipeline to Yanbu and then Bab al-Mandab, and the Gulf terminals themselves — and this week is the first time all three have been simultaneously contested. Mechanism our reader should keep: a hedge is worth nothing if the failure modes correlate, and correlation is what has just happened, because one adversary coalition can now reach the launch point for each. Report the hard numbers rather than the atmosphere — East–West throughput capacity and current flow, Yanbu loadings, transits through Bab al-Mandab this week against the 2023 baseline, Brent and Dubai, and the war-risk premium as a percentage of hull value on each of the three routings, which is the figure that actually decides whether a charterer sails. Then the part Western defence coverage never carries: the countries that lose first are not the buyers but the importers with no strategic reserve and a dollar-denominated fuel bill — Pakistan, Egypt, Bangladesh, Kenya — where a sustained freight and insurance step-up becomes a currency and subsidy crisis within a quarter. Name them and cost it. This is the third and final entry in the pipeline arc (after 09-12 Ankara and 09-13 Maysan) — it is the consolidated economics, so do not re-tell the launcher seizure or the shutdown. SOURCING: The War Zone is single-source and US defence-trade; the writer must verify the Bab al-Mandab and pipeline claims against Lloyd's List, Reuters, EIA or TankerTrackers, and should seek Arab News (SA), Al Jazeera (QA) or Mehr (IR) for the regional read — the feed offers no OIC-region outlet on this specific analysis, which is a feed-side gap worth auditing given Saudi Arabia, Yemen and Iraq are the subjects.

stories.label: NATO nation's arms company hit by second ammo depot fire in one month
stories.summary: A major fire broke out late Friday at an ammunition store run by the Bulgarian arms maker EMCO in Gabrovo province — the second such fire at the company in a month. Write the industrial base, not the sabotage rumour. Lead with the concentration: Bulgaria is one of a very small number of NATO states that still makes Soviet-calibre ammunition at scale, which is precisely what Ukraine's inherited weapons fire, so a single Bulgarian company sits in a supply chain no amount of Western money can reroute quickly. Mechanism our reader will recognise from other sectors: Europe's shell shortage was never a money problem, it was nitrocellulose, presses, certification and magazine space, and those are physical assets measured in years — which is why losing storage at one firm twice in a month is a capacity event rather than an incident. Report what EMCO actually produces, its export licences and volumes, what burned (finished rounds, propellant, or empty magazine space — they are entirely different losses), casualties, and what the Bulgarian interior ministry and prosecutors have said about cause. Then the accountability question with a real history behind it: Bulgarian arms depots have burned before, and the 2011–2020 GRU-linked blasts at Emilian Gebrev's facilities were eventually charged as sabotage — so a sabotage hypothesis is legitimate to report, and it is also exactly what an unverified claim looks like. SOURCING DISCIPLINE, and this is binding: RT is a Russian state outlet with a direct interest in the narrative that Western ammunition supply is burning, and it is the only source in the feed cluster despite eventCoverage of 123. The writer must confirm the fire, the location and the second-incident claim against Bulgarian outlets (BTA, bTV, Dnevnik), Reuters or AFP before printing anything, attribute the sabotage allegation to whoever actually made it, and drop the story entirely if only RT carries it.

stories.label: Crafts from 100 Pakistani villages on display under one roof at Karachi Expo Centre
stories.summary: The 25th Daachi Arts and Crafts Exhibition opened at the Karachi Expo Centre with about 200 stalls carrying work from more than 100 villages — Hala and Multan pottery, Sindhi and Balochi embroidery, ralli quilts. Do not write a culture listing; write the market-access problem it exists to solve. Lead with the distance the goods travelled and what that distance normally costs: a Hala potter or a Tharparkar embroiderer sells through middlemen who take the margin because the producer has no route to a buyer, and a two-day fair is a temporary substitute for a distribution channel that the sector does not have the rest of the year. Mechanism for our reader, which is the structural why: Pakistani handicraft is overwhelmingly home-based female labour, unregistered, uncounted in GDP and outside the labour code — so 'informal' here means no contract, no minimum piece rate and no bargaining position, and the reason craft exports stay small is not demand abroad but the absence of aggregation, certification and freight at the producer end. Report the real economics — what an embroiderer is paid per piece against the Expo Centre retail price, Pakistan's annual handicraft export figure and its trend, what TDAP and SMEDA actually fund, and whether any of the 100 villages sell online or through a cooperative. Then the comparison that makes the point land: India's and Morocco's craft-export programmes are built on artisan registries and geographical-indication marks, and Pakistan's are not — say what that costs. Quote artisans by name, especially women, rather than organisers. Pakistan is an OIC member and Dawn (PK) is the regional source. This is the audit's flagged absence of any non-conflict economy story from Asia or Africa — treat it as economics, and the register must be sober, not celebratory.

stories.label: Xi by his side, Modi warns against 'weaponisation of tech'
stories.summary: At the New Delhi BRICS summit, with Xi Jinping beside him, Modi asked the bloc to recognise the danger of weaponising 'technology and critical minerals'. Lead with who is standing next to whom, because the sentence is aimed in two directions at once and the staging is the reporting: China holds the chokepoint Modi is describing. Write the supply chain, not the summit — we have covered this summit three times and will not cover it again. Mechanism, concretely: China refines roughly nine-tenths of the world's rare earths and holds near-monopoly positions in gallium, germanium and graphite processing, and export-licensing controls on those inputs are now a routine instrument of Chinese statecraft — while the United States runs the mirror-image instrument in the Entity List and the chip-tooling controls that reach any fab using American equipment anywhere. Both are 'weaponisation', and Modi named neither. That is the story: a summit communiqué against chokepoint coercion signed by the two states that own the chokepoints. Report the actual dependency figures with sources, India's own position (it has export-restricted some minerals and is building a rare-earth magnet scheme), and what the declaration text says as against what it omits. Then the stakes for our reader: Indonesia, Malaysia, Turkey and the Gulf are building semiconductor, EV and battery capacity on inputs they do not control, so a licence regime in Beijing or Washington sets the ceiling on industrial policy in Jakarta and Ankara — that is technological sovereignty stated as an arithmetic, and it is why this belongs in tech rather than diplomacy. Multi-source: NDTV and Rediff (both IN), sentiment divergence 0.35. No OIC-region outlet covered this specific event angle in the feed, though Dawn (PK) carried the separate BRICS restraint declaration — note that as a feed-side gap.

stories.label: A misalignment of AI in mathematics
stories.summary: A statement from working mathematicians arguing that what AI labs are optimising for in mathematics is not what mathematics is for — 1,192 points and 1,168 comments on Hacker News, the highest-attention technical item in today's feed. Lead with the misalignment claim stated precisely: benchmark performance rewards producing a correct answer to a closed problem, while mathematics as a discipline produces understanding, definitions and proofs that other humans can check and build on — so a model that saturates competition benchmarks can be simultaneously superhuman on the metric and useless for the practice. Mechanism our technically literate reader will want, not vibes: explain formalisation and why Lean and mathlib matter here — a machine proof that typechecks is verifiable in a way a natural-language proof from a language model is not, which makes the verification gap the actual bottleneck, and it is why 'AI solved an IMO problem' and 'AI advanced number theory' are different claims. Report what the statement actually says, who signed it and what their standing is, what it asks of funders and labs, and the strongest counter-argument from the other side (Lean-assisted collaborations and the equational-theories projects are real results, and the piece must concede them). Then the structural why, which is why this is a story and not a discourse item: research funding and graduate training follow benchmark narratives, so if the metric is wrong the misallocation lands on the next generation of mathematicians — and on departments in Pakistan, Egypt, Iran and Nigeria that cannot afford to chase a compute-defined frontier and would be better served by the formalisation tooling, which is free. SOURCING: the link is the primary document at mathandai.org, surfaced via Hacker News; treat the document as the source, name its signatories, and do not present its claims as established consensus.

stories.label: Beyond full fine-tuning: towards enhanced generalizability in downstream ECG foundation model adaptation
stories.summary: Researchers report that fully fine-tuning an ECG foundation model on a downstream task generalises worse than lighter adaptation methods — the model learns the hospital, not the heart. Lead with that failure mode, because it is the one thing clinicians and engineers both need and neither is told: full fine-tuning on a single site's recordings overwrites the general representation with local artefacts — that site's electrode placement, lead noise, patient mix and device vendor — so the model posts a better score on held-out data from the same hospital and degrades on anyone else's. Mechanism for our reader: parameter-efficient adaptation (LoRA, adapters, linear probing — say which the paper tested) freezes most of the pretrained weights and trains a small number, which structurally limits how much local idiosyncrasy the model can absorb; the constraint is the feature. Report the actual evidence — the datasets and how many sites, in-distribution versus out-of-distribution accuracy for each method, the number of trainable parameters, and whether the gains hold on the arrhythmia classes that are rare and clinically dangerous rather than on aggregate AUC. Then the structural why, which is the reason this belongs in our feed: ECG is the cheapest diagnostic in cardiology and the one most likely to be automated first in health systems with few cardiologists — Pakistan, Egypt, Nigeria, Indonesia — and those systems will deploy models pretrained on North American and European cohorts with local data too scarce for full fine-tuning. A method that adapts well on little data is a health-access fact before it is an ML result; a model that silently learns one hospital is a harm exported. Accepted manuscript with a DOI, not the version of record — say so, and name the authors and institutions.

stories.label: Effects of heat exposure on self-reported heat strain symptoms among pregnant and postpartum women in South Africa
stories.summary: A cohort study in South Africa finds that 14-day average outdoor wet-bulb globe temperature and maximum air temperature are both consistently associated with heat strain symptoms in pregnant and postpartum women, and the associations survive adjustment for covariates. Lead with the fourteen days, because the exposure window is the finding: this is not heatstroke on a record afternoon, it is cumulative load over a fortnight, which means the risk is invisible to every warning system built around single-day thresholds. Mechanism, explained plainly and it is genuinely interesting physiology: pregnancy already runs a raised metabolic rate, expanded plasma volume and a redistributed cardiac output that sends blood to the placenta, so a pregnant woman has less thermoregulatory reserve to spend on skin perfusion and sweating — heat and pregnancy compete for the same circulatory capacity, and the fetus has no independent way to shed heat. Say what the downstream outcomes in the wider literature are (preterm birth, low birthweight, stillbirth) and be careful to mark which this study measured and which it did not. Report the numbers: cohort size, setting, effect estimates per degree, and what WBGT is and why it differs from the temperature on a phone — it folds humidity, radiant heat and wind, which is exactly why it catches what a thermometer misses. Then who is affected and how, concretely: women doing outdoor agricultural or informal work in Limpopo and Mpumalanga, in homes with metal roofs and no cooling, who cannot take a fortnight off — the intervention that follows from a 14-day exposure window is work scheduling and shade, not an emergency alert. This is African science about African women, from a South African cohort, against an audit gap of two Africa articles in three days, both of them security. Name the institutions and the cohort.

stories.label: A multimodal murmuration for immunotherapy
stories.summary: A Nature Medicine piece arguing that predicting who benefits from cancer immunotherapy requires many weak signals read together — imaging, pathology, genomics, circulating markers — rather than the single biomarker the field has spent a decade looking for. Lead with the failure that motivates it: PD-L1 expression and tumour mutational burden are the biomarkers in clinical use, and they are poor enough that most patients given a checkpoint inhibitor do not respond while carrying its real toxicity and its very large price. Mechanism, and the metaphor in the title is the argument: a murmuration has no leader — the behaviour is a property of the interactions, and the claim here is that immunotherapy response is likewise a system state, not a molecule, so combining modalities recovers signal that no single assay holds. Explain why that is technically hard rather than merely fashionable: each modality has its own missingness and batch effects, and a multimodal model trained on a few hundred patients will happily learn the scanner. Report what evidence the authors present, whether it is prospective or retrospective, the effect sizes, and the declared conflicts — the corresponding author reports funding from AstraZeneca and Roche and sits on a Roche trial steering committee, which the piece must state, because these are the companies selling the drugs a better biomarker would ration. Then the access point our reader should be given: a multimodal predictor needs an MRI, digitised pathology, a sequencing panel and the informatics to fuse them, so a method that improves patient selection in Barcelona can simultaneously widen the gap for a hospital in Cairo or Lahore where the single cheap assay is all there is — better prediction is not automatically better access. This is a perspective piece, not a trial; label it as argument and attribute throughout.

stories.label: Bahrain won't attend meeting on Hormuz in Oman
stories.summary: Bahrain has refused to attend Monday's Iran–Gulf meeting in Muscat on the Strait of Hormuz until diplomatic ties with Tehran are restored, and a senior Iranian official says nothing will be signed there anyway. Lead with the empty chair, not the meeting: the Gulf is being asked to negotiate the security of the waterway all of its exports pass through, and one of its members will not sit in the room. Mechanism for the reader: Oman is the only GCC state that has kept channels to Tehran open through every rupture, which is why Muscat and not Riyadh hosts this — mediation is a capability, and it is unevenly distributed across the Gulf. Explain what a Hormuz arrangement would actually have to cover (transit notification, escort rules, insurance war-risk zones, who de-mines) and why none of it works without Bahrain, which hosts the US Fifth Fleet. Report Pezeshkian's line that the region does not need the US as its 'policeman' alongside the fact that Bahrain's refusal is itself a US-aligned position — set the two against each other rather than picking one. Name who is attending and who is not. Bahrain, Iran, Oman, Saudi Arabia and Qatar are all OIC members and the feed carries Dawn (PK), Al Jazeera (QA) and Middle East Eye — regional coverage is present; do not rest the piece on Western wires. Distinct from our 09-12 pipeline and Trump-claims coverage: this is the diplomacy of the waterway, not the war.

stories.label: Sweden election: Far right eyes power for 1st time
stories.summary: Swedes vote today in an election that could put the Sweden Democrats — a party with roots in the 1980s white-nationalist movement — inside government for the first time, after four years of propping up Kristersson's minority coalition from outside. Lead with the threshold being crossed, not the horse race: the question is not whether the far right is popular (it already is, it has been the kingmaker since 2022) but whether the cordon sanitaire that kept it out of ministries finally goes. Mechanism to explain: Sweden's proportional system with a 4% threshold makes coalition arithmetic everything, so a party can set policy for years without holding a portfolio — the Tidö Agreement already gave the SD influence over migration and policing without the responsibility. Report concretely what the SD would control if it enters cabinet, and what its programme says about citizenship revocation, family reunification, and the roughly 800,000 Swedish residents born in Muslim-majority countries who are the explicit subject of that programme. Who is affected: immigrant and Muslim communities in Malmö, Rinkeby and Rosengård, whose status is the campaign's central issue and who are rarely quoted in coverage of it — quote them. Give the results and the seat maths if they are in by writing time; if not, write the stakes and say plainly that counting is under way. Sources diverge sharply in framing (DW 0.30, TRT 0.07) — Al Jazeera and TRT will cover the migration plank that DW treats as background; use both.

stories.label: Femi Fani-Kayode Reacts To Murder Of Michael Taiwo, James Nwankwo In SouthAfrica
stories.summary: Two Nigerians — Bishop Michael Taiwo Fakunle, shot at his Johannesburg home on 4 September after a series of threats, and James Uchechukwu Nwankwo — were killed in South Africa, and a former Nigerian foreign-affairs minister is demanding Abuja respond. Lead with the two named men and the threats that preceded the first killing, because a warning that was ignored is the accountability fact here: the question for the South African Police Service is what was done between the threats and the shooting. Mechanism, and it is the structural why: roughly 800,000 Nigerians and other African migrants live in South Africa inside an economy with the world's highest measured unemployment, where organised movements like Operation Dudula have made migrants the explanation for it — so xenophobic violence there is not random crime, it is a politics with organisations, spokesmen and a body count that has been accumulating since 2008. Report what SAPS has said, whether anyone is charged, what the Nigerian mission in Pretoria has done, and what came of the compensation and repatriation promises after the 2019 and 2021 waves. SOURCING: the feed carries only Nairaland, a Nigerian forum reproducing Fani-Kayode's statement — that is a politician's statement, not established fact. The writer must verify both deaths against South African outlets and Nigerian wires (Premium Times, Vanguard, NAN) before printing, and drop any detail that cannot be confirmed. Nigeria is an OIC member; Nairaland (NG) is the only regional outlet the feed offers on this event and it is a weak one — log that as a feed-side gap. This is the audit's flagged Africa gap: give African actors and victims their names.

stories.label: LP chieftain sues UNN over alleged refusal to release Peter Obi's academic records
stories.summary: A Labour Party figure has gone to court against the University of Nigeria, Nsukka and its vice-chancellor for refusing a freedom-of-information request for Peter Obi's academic records. Do not write this as a scandal about Obi — write it as a test of whether Nigeria's Freedom of Information Act reaches a public university at all. Lead with the mechanism: the FOI Act of 2011 obliges public institutions to release records within seven days or give reasons, but universities and state bodies have spent a decade arguing they are not covered, and courts have split — so every suit like this is the statute being litigated into existence one respondent at a time. Explain what the applicant asked for, on what date, what UNN answered, and what remedy the court can actually order. Then the structural why for our reader: candidate-credential disputes have decided or shadowed Nigerian elections before (the certificate cases against Tinubu and others), and the reason they fester is that the records custodian, not the candidate, is the chokepoint — an institution that will not answer an FOI request makes verification impossible and rumour cheap. Note the applicant is a former factional LP spokesman, so his motive is political; say so plainly and keep the story on the disclosure duty, not the insinuation. Nigeria is an OIC member and Premium Times (NG) is the regional outlet — original single-source reporting from a credible investigative newsroom; attribute to it throughout. Second of two Africa entries this cycle against a flagged continental gap.

stories.label: The Language of Terrorism Since 9/11
stories.summary: Twenty-five years on, the world's media have quietly retreated from the word 'terrorism' while governments have expanded it — and the gap between the two is where a great deal of law now lives. Lead with the asymmetry itself: newsrooms adopted 'militant', 'gunman', 'armed group' precisely because the older word carried a judgement they could not source, while legislatures went the other way and wrote the judgement into statute, where it triggers powers no ordinary criminal charge does. Mechanism, and it is the reason this belongs beside our 09-12 piece on the Alien Terrorist Removal Court: a terrorism designation is an administrative act, made before any adversarial test, that unlocks asset freezes, secret evidence, proscription of membership and removal without an ordinary hearing — so the word is not a description, it is a switch. Report concretely how many entities are on the major designation lists now against 2001, which categories have been added (environmental and animal-rights groups, protest movements, in some states entire diaspora charities), and who reviews a designation once made. Who is affected: Muslim organisations and charities most of all, but increasingly anyone a government finds inconvenient — and the reader should be given the general rule, not only the familiar cases. Treat this as reported argument, not opinion: every claim must come off the New Lines piece and its named sources, attributed to it, with no editorialising added. High reader relevance on the 9/11 anniversary week, which is also today's public-attention signal.

stories.label: Iraq seizes drone launch platform used in Saudi oil pipeline attack
stories.summary: Iraqi security forces say they have located and seized the launch platform used to strike Saudi Arabia's East–West pipeline, with Lt Gen Saad Maan announcing it through the state news agency INA. Lead with the object, because a seized platform is the first physical evidence in a story that has so far been entirely claims: it establishes the launch was from Iraqi soil, in Maysan, and it puts Baghdad in possession of something that can be traced. Mechanism and why it matters beyond one strike: the East–West line exists so Saudi crude can reach the Red Sea without passing Hormuz, and drones launched from Iraq defeat that hedge by making both routes vulnerable to one actor — we reported that logic on 09-12 from Ankara's statement; this is the evidence stage, so advance it rather than repeating it. Report what the platform actually is (vehicle-mounted rail, fixed frame, launch tubes — say which), who Iraq names or declines to name, whether any arrests followed, and what the Popular Mobilisation Forces' position is, since the accusation runs toward groups inside the Iraqi state's own security architecture. Then the economics: pipeline throughput before and after, current Brent, and Red Sea and Gulf war-risk premiums. Accountability: a state that seizes the launcher but names no one has answered half the question — say which half. Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Turkey are OIC members; the feed carries Al Jazeera (QA) and TRT World (TR), so regional coverage is present. Second entry in the pipeline arc — do not re-tell the shutdown.

stories.label: Tanker hit by projectile in Strait of Hormuz -- UKMTO
stories.summary: The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre has logged a tanker struck by a projectile inside the Strait of Hormuz — no vessel name, no flag, no casualty figure yet. Lead with the location, because that is the whole story: a hit inside the strait itself, not off Yemen and not at a Saudi terminal, is the third of the three export routes being closed, and roughly a fifth of the world's seaborne oil passes through a channel whose shipping lanes are two miles wide. Mechanism for the reader: the market does not move on barrels lost, it moves on insurance — a UKMTO incident report is the trigger that repricing war-risk cover keys off, and a premium rise of a fraction of a percent of hull value per voyage is what actually decides whether a charterer sails. Report the war-risk rate before and after if it can be obtained, the Brent and Dubai benchmarks, and how many laden tankers transited this week against the normal count. Then the human fact that gets omitted: crews on these ships are overwhelmingly Filipino, Indian, Bangladeshi and Pakistani seafarers who cannot decline the voyage, and they are the people a projectile actually reaches — find out who was aboard. SOURCING DISCIPLINE: the only feed source is TASS, a Russian state agency with an interest in a high oil price, and it is reporting a UKMTO advisory — the writer must pull the UKMTO advisory itself and a shipping wire (Lloyd's List, Reuters, TradeWinds) and print nothing that is not in them; if the advisory cannot be found, drop the story. Iran, Oman and the UAE are OIC states and the feed carries NO regional outlet on this incident — log that as a feed-side gap.

stories.label: OpenAI's Altman rules out 2026 IPO as AI safety takes priority
stories.summary: Sam Altman has ruled out an OpenAI listing this year — a September IPO had been in preparation — telling Fortune that going public now would make it harder to prioritise safety over shareholders. Lead with the reversal and its timing, not the sentiment: a company that was weeks from a filing has stood down, in the same week its rivals' chief executives all called publicly for the race to slow. Mechanism, and this is what our reader should take away: a public company acquires a fiduciary duty to shareholders and a quarterly disclosure cadence, which is exactly the machinery that makes 'we delayed a model' an actionable disappointment — so Altman's stated reason is a real one, and it is also a reason that has always been true and did not stop the preparation. Report what OpenAI's capital position actually is, because that is the alternative explanation the piece must weigh: the compute commitments, the Microsoft arrangement, the private-round valuations, and how long the company can fund training runs without public markets. Note that critics (MoneyControl among them) read the industry-wide slowdown call as cover for an IPO that the market would not have taken at the asked price — give the reader the facts to judge that, not a verdict. Structural why: whether the frontier labs are financed by private capital or public markets decides who can ever see their numbers, and therefore whether any of this is auditable from outside. Distinct from our 09-12 Amodei-slowdown piece: that was the essay, this is the balance sheet. Do not re-argue the slowdown debate.

stories.label: From smartphone to luxury tech: iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro — why Apple may be pushing the iPhone further upmarket
stories.summary: Apple's new line and the carrier promotions around it point one way: the iPhone is being repositioned as luxury hardware, and T-Mobile's 'free' iPhone 18 Pro is the tell. Do not write a launch story — write the financing. Lead with what 'free' actually means: a trade-in plus a two-year bill-credit schedule on the most expensive plan, which is a consumer loan with an early-termination penalty, structured so the phone's real price never appears on a receipt. Mechanism our reader will recognise instantly: Apple's unit sales have been flat for years, so revenue growth has to come from average selling price and services, and the carrier subsidy is the instrument that raises the sticker while hiding it from the buyer. Then the part no Western coverage carries: outside the US and Gulf there is no subsidy — an iPhone 18 Pro in Karachi, Lagos, Cairo or Jakarta is bought outright in cash or on local instalment credit at rates several times a US bill credit, so the same device is one month's salary in one market and a rounding error in another, and Apple's upmarket move quietly widens that gap. Report the actual prices across markets in local currency and as a share of median monthly income, the trade-in and plan conditions, and what the 'iPhone Duo' actually is rather than what the rumour cycle says. Khaleej Times carries the UAE launch and resale timing; use it for the Gulf figures. Avoid gadget-review register entirely.

stories.label: Review: A Vision of a Future Where Machines Fight Wars
stories.summary: Frank Kendall — until recently the civilian official who ran US Air Force acquisition, and before that the Pentagon's chief weapons buyer — argues in a new book that machines will and should make some decisions to strike people and infrastructure. Lead with who is saying it, not that a book exists: this is the man who signed the cheques arguing that the human-in-the-loop requirement is a luxury the US cannot keep, and that is a procurement position with a budget behind it, not a thought experiment. Mechanism to explain precisely, because the debate is usually conducted in slogans: 'autonomy' in a weapon means the target-recognition and engagement decision happens onboard, and the reason commanders want it is latency and jamming — a datalink to a human operator is the thing an adversary attacks first, so the pressure toward autonomy comes from electronic warfare, not from ideology. That is the same arithmetic as our 09-12 drone-boat piece: when links fail, the machine either decides or is useless. Report what Kendall actually proposes, what he concedes, and what the current US policy (DoD Directive 3000.09) requires — then the accountability question that no autonomy doctrine has answered: when an autonomous system kills the wrong people, who is the defendant. Who is affected: populations under drone and loitering-munition warfare now — Yemen, Gaza, Sudan, the Sahel — where the systems are already deployed and the review procedures are not. Treat the book as the source and attribute to it; do not present Kendall's forecasts as findings.

stories.label: AI, Robotics and the Coming Economic, Military, and Political Revolutions
stories.summary: An argument that China's coupling of AI to physical robotics — not chatbots, but factories, ports and munitions lines — is the transformation that matters, and that it lands on economics, military power and domestic politics at once. Lead with the hinge the piece turns on: a model that only writes text competes with white-collar labour, while a model attached to an actuator competes with the manufacturing base a country's power actually rests on — which is why the interesting number is installed industrial robots per 10,000 workers, and why China's has passed Germany's and Japan's. Report those figures and their sources rather than asserting a trend. Mechanism for our reader, who follows this as a strategic question: robotics compresses the gap between civilian and military production, because the same automated line that makes appliances makes drones and shell casings, so 'industrial capacity' stops being a peacetime statistic and becomes a mobilisation rate — that is the concrete reason Washington and Beijing both now treat factory automation as a defence programme. Then the part the piece should not be allowed to skip: what this means for countries that are neither — Indonesia, Bangladesh, Egypt, Morocco built development strategies on cheap manufacturing labour, and automation at this cost curve removes the rung they were climbing. Follows our 09-12 piece on the $4,000 Chinese quadruped without repeating its cost-curve argument; this is the strategic frame around it. This is analysis, not reporting — attribute every claim to The Diplomat and its named sources, and label forecasts as forecasts.

stories.label: MP hooch tragedy: Wanted accused caught after encounter in Sagar; 19 held so far
stories.summary: Sixteen people are dead from illicit liquor in Sagar district, Madhya Pradesh; 19 are in custody and a 21-year-old carrying a ₹30,000 bounty was shot in the leg in a police 'encounter'. Lead with the poison, not the manhunt: hooch deaths are methanol deaths, and methanol is not merely a contaminant — it is added deliberately to bulk out ethanol because it is cheap and industrial supply is poorly controlled. Explain the mechanism plainly, because it is what makes these deaths preventable: methanol itself is relatively harmless until the liver's alcohol dehydrogenase converts it to formaldehyde and then formic acid, which blinds and kills over 12 to 24 hours — which is why victims arrive feeling fine and die later, and why the antidote is either fomepizole or, remarkably, ethanol, both of which occupy the same enzyme. A district hospital that knows this and has either drug on the shelf saves most of a cohort; one that does not, loses them. Report how many of the 16 died before reaching hospital, whether any were treated with ethanol or fomepizole, and how many survivors have lost sight. Then the accountability layer: who supplied the methanol and from which industrial channel, since that is the regulated link in the chain, and what Madhya Pradesh's excise department knew about this trade. Finally, treat the 'encounter' with the scepticism it earns — a suspect shot in the leg while in police custody is a standard formula in Indian police accounts, and the piece should say who investigates it. NOTE FOR THE AUDIT: the feed carried no Nature, Quanta, SciDev.Net, STAT or Carbon Brief item this cycle — this is the only science-substrate story available, so the science floor is met at one, not two, on feed supply rather than editorial choice.
